# Push policy at the git proxy

## What to build

Enable `git push` through the Rakazo git proxy, enforced by the server. A bot may only:

- create new branches under its repository's `branchPrefix` (for example `refs/heads/rakazo/docs-bot/…`);
- fast-forward branches it created earlier.

Everything else is refused before any bytes reach the host. That covers the default branch, other people's branches, tags, deletions, non-fast-forward (force) updates, and refs outside the prefix. Refusals come back as normal git output (`remote: rakazo: …` and `! [remote rejected] … (rakazo policy)`), so the bot can read and act on them.

A branch counts as bot-owned once the host's own report confirms a create succeeded; the proxy then writes a `BotRepositoryBranch` row. Every decision, allowed or refused, goes to the audit log.

This replaces the temporary refusal `rakazo: pushing is not available yet` that the fetch-path slice left in `apps/api/src/git-proxy.ts`. It also adds a hook so the GitLab push-approval slice can add one more check without rewriting the policy.

Already in the codebase:

- **`apps/api/src/git-proxy.ts`:**
  - `mountGitProxyRoutes(app, { prisma, secrets, codeHosts, fetch? })` serves `/git/:repo/info/refs`, `/git/:repo/git-upload-pack` and `/git/:repo/git-receive-pack`.
  - It handles Basic auth, `resolveGitProxyGrant`, the 401/403 text/plain responses, upstream forwarding with `duplex: "half"`, and the current receive-pack refusal.
- **Grants (`packages/adapters/src/git-proxy-grants.ts`):** `resolveGitProxyGrant(prisma, token, bindingId)` returns `{ grant, run, binding, connection }`.
- **Models:**
  - `BotRepositoryBranch { id, spaceId, userId, botRepositoryId, ref, createdByRunId, createdAt, @@unique([botRepositoryId, ref]) }`.
  - `BotRepository` holds `branchPrefix` (like `rakazo/docs-bot/`).
- **Branch helper (`packages/core/src/code-host-branch.ts`):** `isBotBranchRef(ref, prefix)`.
- **Emulator (`packages/adapters/src/code-host-emulator.ts`):** `CodeHostEmulator` serves real smart HTTP through `git http-backend`, with `http.receivepack=true`. It also has `refs(fullPath)` and `hasGit()`.
- **Contract (`packages/adapter-kit/src/code-host.ts`):** `CodeHostProvider` is implemented by `GitlabCodeHostProvider` (`gitlab-code-host.ts`) and `GithubCodeHostProvider` (`github-code-host.ts`).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `CODE-HOST-INTEGRATION-PRD.md` section 9 "Push rules" and section 10 "Git proxy" (the refusal example).
- `apps/api/src/git-proxy.ts` — the whole file, which you will extend.
- `packages/db/src/audit-events.ts` (lines 19–50) — `recordAuditEvent`. Metadata takes scalars only, and content-like keys are dropped.
- `packages/adapters/src/code-host-emulator.ts` — the git backend, to extend with ancestry checks.
- `packages/adapters/src/code-host-conformance.test.ts` — the shared provider suite; add `isAncestor` cases to it.
- The git protocol docs (pkt-line, report-status, side-band) at https://git-scm.com/docs/pack-protocol and https://git-scm.com/docs/http-protocol. Summary:
  - A pkt-line is a 4-hex-digit length that includes the 4 header bytes. `0000` is a flush.
  - A receive-pack request is a list of command pkt-lines, `<old-sha> <new-sha> <refname>`, where the first line also carries `\0<capabilities>`. A flush follows, then the packfile. There is no packfile when every command is a delete.
  - The response is a report-status: `unpack ok`, then `ok <ref>` or `ng <ref> <reason>` per ref, then a flush. When the client sent `side-band-64k` (or `side-band`), the report is wrapped in band 1 pkt-lines (first payload byte `\x01`) and messages travel on band 2 (`\x02`, shown by git as `remote: …`).

## Patterns to follow

**Policy as a pure function (easy to unit test):**
```ts
// apps/api/src/git-push-policy.ts
export type PushCommand = { oldSha: string; newSha: string; ref: string };
export type PushDecision = { ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string; perRef: Record<string, string> };
export function checkPushCommands(commands: PushCommand[], input: { branchPrefix: string; ownedRefs: Set<string> }): PushDecision
```
Rules, applied to every command. The whole push is refused if any command fails:

1. No tags (`refs/tags/…`) and no refs outside `refs/heads/`. Message: `rakazo: bots can only push branches they created under <branchPrefix>`.
2. `isBotBranchRef(ref, branchPrefix)` must hold. If not, use the same message as rule 1.
3. Deletes (`newSha` is all zeros) are refused: `rakazo: bots cannot delete branches`.
4. Creates (`oldSha` is all zeros) are allowed.
5. Updates must target a ref in `ownedRefs`. If not: `rakazo: <branch> was not created by this bot`.
6. Updates must be fast-forwards. The route checks this separately, after the pack is indexed: `rakazo: <branch> can only be fast-forwarded (no force pushes)`.

The route also runs an extra check hook, `extraPushChecks?: Array<(ctx) => Promise<PushDecision>>`, which deps may pass. Leave it empty in this slice; the GitLab push-approval slice adds one.

**Audit:**
```ts
await recordAuditEvent({ action: "code.push", actor: { type: "bot", id: run.botId, label: botName },
  spaceId: run.spaceId, runId: run.id, outcome: "success" | "denied" | "failure",
  target: { type: "repository", id: binding.id, label: binding.fullPath },
  metadata: { provider: connection.provider, refs: commands.map(c => c.ref).join(","), reason: shortReason } });
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/adapter-kit/src/code-host.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: add `isAncestor(connection: CodeHostConnectionRef, repo: CodeHostRepository, ancestorSha: string, descendantSha: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<boolean>` to `CodeHostProvider`.

### UPDATE the adapters and the emulator
- **GitHub (`github-code-host.ts`):** `GET {api}/repos/{fullPath}/compare/{ancestor}...{descendant}`. Return true when `status` is `ahead` or `identical`. Return false on `behind`, `diverged` or 404.
- **GitLab (`gitlab-code-host.ts`):** `GET /api/v4/projects/:id/repository/merge_base?refs[]=<a>&refs[]=<b>`. Return true when the response `id` equals the ancestor; return false on 404/400.
- **Emulator:** serve both endpoints by running `git -C <bare> merge-base --is-ancestor a b` and `git -C <bare> merge-base a b`.
- **Conformance:** add a case where a seeded commit is an ancestor of a later pushed commit, and the reverse is false.

### CREATE `apps/api/src/git-pkt.ts` (+ tests)
- **IMPLEMENT** small streaming helpers:
  - `readPktLines(reader)`: reads command pkt-lines up to the first flush and returns `{ lines: Uint8Array[], consumed: Uint8Array /* exact bytes read, incl. flush */, rest: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> /* remaining body */ }`. It must handle pkt-lines split across chunks. Cap the command section at 1 MiB and 1000 commands.
  - `parseCommands(lines)` returns `{ commands: PushCommand[], capabilities: string[] }`.
  - `encodePkt(text | bytes)`, `flushPkt()`.
  - `receivePackRefusal({ commands, message, perRef, sideBand: boolean })` returns the response body bytes:
    - With `sideBand`: a band-2 pkt carrying `rakazo: …\n`, then band-1 pkts carrying the report pkt-lines `unpack ok\n` and `ng <ref> rakazo policy\n` per command, then their flush, then a final flush.
    - Without `sideBand`: the report pkt-lines directly.
    - Content type: `application/x-git-receive-pack-result`, status 200.
  - `parseReportStatus(stream, sideBand)`: tees the upstream response and resolves to `Map<ref, "ok" | string /*ng reason*/>`.
  - `addNoThinCapability(advertisement)`: rewrites the first ref advertisement pkt of an `info/refs?service=git-receive-pack` response, the one after `# service=…` and its flush, so its capability list includes `no-thin`. It recomputes the pkt length and passes everything else through unchanged. With `no-thin` advertised, clients send self-contained packs.
- **VALIDATE**: `pnpm vitest run apps/api/src/git-pkt.test.ts`. Test with real bytes captured from `git push` against the emulator, plus split-chunk cases.

### CREATE `apps/api/src/git-push-policy.ts` (+ tests)
- **IMPLEMENT** `checkPushCommands` as above, and `checkFastForwards`.
- `checkFastForwards({ commands, packFile, provider, ref, repo })` works like this:
  1. For each update (old is non-zero), walk commits from `newSha` through the indexed pack. To index the pack:
     - spool it to a temp file with a 512 MiB cap; if over the cap, refuse with `rakazo: push is too large`;
     - `git init --bare <tmp>`;
     - `git -C <tmp> index-pack --stdin < packFile`;
     - read commits with `git -C <tmp> cat-file --batch` in one process, parsing `parent <sha>` lines.
  2. If the walk reaches `oldSha`, it is a fast-forward.
  3. Commits missing from the pack are boundary commits. If the walk didn't reach `oldSha`, call `provider.isAncestor(ref, repo, oldSha, boundary)` for the boundaries, up to 20 of them; any true means fast-forward.
  4. Cap the walk at 10,000 commits.
  5. Remove the temp dir in `finally`.
- **GOTCHA**:
  - If `git` is not installed on the API host (`hasGit()` from `@rakazo/adapters`), allow creates. Refuse updates with `rakazo: updating an existing branch needs git on the Rakazo server; push a new branch under <prefix> instead`. That keeps the failure safe and explicit.
  - Use `execFile`/`spawn` with argv arrays only, never a shell string.

### UPDATE `apps/api/src/git-proxy.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `GET info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`: forward as for upload-pack, but stream the response through `addNoThinCapability`.
  - `POST git-receive-pack`:
    1. `const { lines, consumed, rest } = await readPktLines(body.getReader())`, then `parseCommands`.
    2. If `content-encoding: gzip` is present, decompress first with `DecompressionStream("gzip")`.
    3. Load `ownedRefs` with `prisma.botRepositoryBranch.findMany({ where: { botRepositoryId: binding.id }, select: { ref: true } })`.
    4. `checkPushCommands`. If it refuses: cancel `rest`, audit `denied`, return `receivePackRefusal`.
    5. If any command is an update: spool `rest` to a temp file and run `checkFastForwards`. Refuse or audit the same way. The forwarded body is then `consumed` followed by the temp file stream. Otherwise it is `consumed` followed by `rest`, streamed.
    6. Run `extraPushChecks`, if any.
    7. Forward upstream and tee the response:
       - one branch streams to the client;
       - the other goes to `parseReportStatus`;
       - when it resolves, record each `ok` create with `prisma.botRepositoryBranch.createMany({ data: [...], skipDuplicates: true })` (`createdByRunId: run.id`), then audit `success` for the ok refs and `failure` for any ng refs.
  - The `sideBand` flag comes from the client's capabilities (`side-band-64k` or `side-band`).
- **GOTCHA**:
  - Only record ownership after the host confirms `ok`. If a teammate created the same branch first, the host refuses the bot's create, because its `old` (zeros) is stale, and the branch never becomes bot-owned.
  - Never record an update as a create.
  - Keep request and response streaming; buffer nothing except the command section and the spooled pack for updates.

### Tests (`apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts`, `describe.skipIf(!hasGit())`)
Run both GitLab and GitHub emulators with the API's proxy served on a real port, and clone through the proxy with a grant, as in `apps/api/src/git-proxy.test.ts`. Use the binding's `branchPrefix` of `rakazo/docs-bot/`. Cases:

1. `git push origin HEAD:rakazo/docs-bot/fix` succeeds, a `BotRepositoryBranch` row exists, and the emulator's `refs()` shows the branch.
2. A second commit plus push to the same branch (fast-forward) succeeds.
3. `git push --force` of a rewritten commit to that branch is refused, and stderr contains `can only be fast-forwarded`.
4. `git push origin HEAD:main` is refused, and stderr contains `rakazo: bots can only push branches they created under rakazo/docs-bot/` and `[remote rejected]`. Host `main` is unchanged.
5. A push to `rakazo/docs-bot/x` where the host already has that branch, not bot-owned (create it directly in the bare repo first), is refused with `was not created by this bot`.
6. `git push origin --delete rakazo/docs-bot/fix` is refused.
7. `git push origin v1` (a tag) is refused.
8. A push with two refs where one is bad leaves both unchanged on the host.
9. Every case writes exactly one `code.push` audit event with the right outcome. Mock `recordAuditEvent` or use the installed store.

Also add unit tests for `checkPushCommands` covering every rule, and for `parseReportStatus` with and without side-band.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Creates under `refs/heads/<branchPrefix>` are forwarded, and the branch becomes bot-owned only after the host reports `ok`.
- [ ] Updates are forwarded only for bot-owned branches and only as fast-forwards. Force pushes are refused.
- [ ] Default branch, other branches, tags, deletions and refs outside the prefix are refused. The client sees `remote: rakazo: …` and `[remote rejected] … (rakazo policy)`, and nothing reaches the host.
- [ ] A multi-ref push is all-or-nothing at the proxy.
- [ ] Every decision is audited as `code.push` with outcome `success`, `denied` or `failure`.
- [ ] The `info/refs` advertisement for receive-pack carries `no-thin`.
- [ ] Without git on the API host, updates are refused safely with a clear message and creates still work.
- [ ] Tests pass: `pnpm vitest run apps/api/src/git-pkt.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push-policy.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts packages/adapters/src/code-host-conformance.test.ts`

## Validation commands

```bash
pnpm lint && pnpm check
pnpm vitest run apps/api/src/git-pkt.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push-policy.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts apps/api/src/git-proxy.test.ts packages/adapters/src/code-host-conformance.test.ts
```
